title: Nonlinear tunnel oscillations of light in spherical Bragg resonators
abstract: A weakly nonlinear regime of radial tunneling is theoretically considered for a light wave in a spherical dielectric Bragg resonator containing a set of ``shell'' eigenmodes (both TE and TM) with different azimuthal numbers $l\geq 1$, which are concentrated near a defect of the Bragg structure, several layers away from the origin. A single radial mode with $l=1$ is present at the resonator center, either TM or TE. Nonlinearity of the Kerr type in the main approximation is actual for the central mode only, while all the shell modes remain in the linear regime. The tunneling occurs between the central mode and the shell $l=1$ mode of the same symmetry. Nontrivial part of the dynamics of optical field is described by a Hamiltonian system of ordinary differential equations for complex vectors ${\bf C}_{1}(t)$ and ${\bf C}_{2}(t)$, which determine the magnitude and spatial orientation of the wave structures at the center and at the shell, respectively. Depending on ``asymmetry parameter'' of tunnel coupling, the system demonstrates different variants of nonlinear behavior.
summary: This paper models the nonlinear tunneling of light in a spherical dielectric Bragg resonator by deriving a coupled Hamiltonian system of ODEs. The analysis focuses on the interaction between a central mode and surrounding 'shell' modes. It demonstrates how Kerr-type nonlinearity modifies the wave dynamics, providing insights into nonlinear wave propagation in structured optical cavities.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates the weakly nonlinear regime of radial tunneling of light within a spherical dielectric Bragg resonator.
main_result: The dynamics are described by a coupled Hamiltonian system of ODEs for the field coefficients, showing that nonlinearity significantly alters the tunneling behavior compared to the linear case.
method: The analysis employs a variational method on the Lagrangian structure to derive effective nonlinear coefficients, leading to a Hamiltonian system of ordinary differential equations.
model_or_system: The system is a spherical dielectric Bragg resonator containing a central radial mode and multiple 'shell' eigenmodes. The dynamics are governed by coupled ODEs for the complex field coefficients $C_1(t)$ and $C_2(t)$.
key_observables: The coefficients $C_1(t)$ and $C_2(t)$ determining the field magnitude and orientation at the center and the shell, respectively; the action $I = |\vec{C}_1|^2 + |\vec{C}_2|^2$.
important_parameters: The 'asymmetry parameter' of the tunnel coupling, and the effective Kerr coefficients $	ilde{\alpha}$ and $	ilde{ eta}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a weakly nonlinear regime, treating the central mode as Kerr-type nonlinear while the shell modes remain linear. It also assumes a locally isotropic, spatially nonuniform dielectric medium.
figures_summary: Figures 1 and 2 illustrate examples of localized linear solutions for TE and TM modes, showing the field structure near central and shell defects.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the linear theory and the Hamiltonian formulation for the field evolution. It then derives the coupled nonlinear ODEs for the mode coefficients, analyzes the resulting Hamiltonian structure, and discusses the physical implications of the nonlinear coupling.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it models nonlinear wave dynamics (tunneling) in structured dielectric media, which can be analogous to cavity QED or nonlinear photonics systems.
